extra.note: Both sp.causal_forest.average_treatment_effect and grf::average_treatment_effect report the AIPW doubly-robust ATE/ATT, and since v1.21 they use the identical operator for both: the ATE score is grf's influence function and the ATT is grf's plug-in CATE average over the treated arm plus a Hajek-normalised doubly-robust correction, with the two variance components summed. Fed grf's own forest outputs, StatsPAI reproduces grf::get_scores elementwise to 2.3e-14 and grf's ATE/ATT estimate and std.err to 1e-15 (tests/reference_parity/test_grf_aipw_operator_parity.py), so the rows below isolate forest RNG rather than any formula difference. On this clean-overlap DGP the StatsPAI row uses clip=0.25, consistent with the known e(X) support [0.30,0.70], and agrees with grf within combined Monte Carlo error. A multi-seed clean-overlap pytest guard checks AIPW truth recovery for both ATE and ATT. The former NSW-DW stress case is now tracked in the Track B robustness sweep.
